item.title: Zimbro House / Stemmer Rodrigues Arquitetura
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: Casa Zimbro was born from the search for an architecture in continuity with the landscape, where the construction does not impose itself on its surroundings but rather integrates with them in a natural and sensitive way. Sited between the lake and the garden, the house is designed in a light and welcoming manner, shaping itself as a refuge that invites both contemplation and gathering.

item.title: Nooba Building / Saraiva + Associados
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: Located on the south bank of the Tagus River in Barreiro, Nooba is conceived as a new residential neighborhood shaped by its proximity to the estuary and the profound urban transformation underway in the south bank's former industrial areas. The project occupies a strategic position within a broad process of urban and environmental regeneration, where new public spaces, mobility infrastructure, and ecological corridors redefine the city's relationship with the river. Its planning framework responds to this metropolitan condition by proposing a neighborhood that balances density with openness, positioning housing as the driver of daily urban life and reinforcing continuity with the revitalized waterfront.

item.title: Zamalanda Park on the Nervión Riverbanks / Burgos & Garrido arquitectos
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: The area surrounding the Portu Dock in Barakaldo is a vast, empty space that bears the traces of its history. Although blurred, it is a place of great beauty and extraordinary potential, offering splendid views over the Nervión estuary from its upper level and a lush, wild horizontal landscape on its lower level.

item.title: The Public Kitchen: How Asian Markets Turn Eating Into Civic Life
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Yeung
item.description: In many Asian cities, eating has never belonged entirely to the private home. It spills into markets, hawker centers, street stalls, and wholesale districts embedded within larger buildings or areas. These are places where the city exchanges information and watches other people pass through. They are not restaurants in the conventional sense, nor are they simply markets. In some way, their vibrancy and usage reflect the society's conditions at that moment. They are public kitchens: shared infrastructures where domestic routines are partially transferred into collective space.

item.title: Housing on top of the petrol station / Gut Deubelbeiss Nill Architekten
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: The project is situated in Emmenbrücke, a town just outside Lucerne. Set within an industrial and high-traffic environment, the building marks the start of the row of houses by Emmenbrücke railway station. Nestled between the railway tracks and the main road, the ground floor houses a petrol station, while the six stories above provide residential apartments.

item.title: WeDoctor Green Valley / gad
item.dc:creator: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang
item.description: Located in the Information Port area of Xiaoshan Economic and Technological Development Zone, Hangzhou, WeHealth Green Valley spans four adjacent plots developed as a single unified phase, with a total construction area of approximately 580,000 square meters. Serving as the headquarters for WeHealth Group and a digital health cluster, the project is envisioned as a city-level public vehicle driven by "publicness".

item.title: Maribyrnong I House / Studio Ceravolo
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: This alterations and additions project to a Californian bungalow welcomes an abundance of natural light and celebrates the passage of time throughout the day. Briefed with renovating and extending a Californian bungalow, we opted to move away from formal expectations and create a project attuned to the present and to the needs of a young family.

item.title: Achime Bagel Store / JOJOWORKSHOP
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: Achime Bagel is a neighborhood bakery located in Munjeong-dong, Seoul. The project began with the idea of creating a small space that could gently accompany the beginning of each day. The bakery prepares and sells its bagels within the same day, and Jojo Workshop sought to translate this simple and diligent attitude into the interior.

item.title: Hermitage House C70 / ASMD Taller Arquitectura
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: Ermita C70 transforms a 1960s house in the historic center of Mérida through an operation of subtraction: demolishing part of the built volume to recover the void as a source of light, ventilation, and social life.

item.title: C.E. House / Dall'Ovo Magalhães Arquitetura
item.dc:creator: Susanna Moreira
item.description: A mountain house that blurs the boundaries between living and contemplating. Sited on a plateau, between rolling lawns and the forest that climbs up the slope, the house sits as if it has belonged to the landscape for a long time. The horizontal, discreet, and elongated volume follows the natural slope of the ground — and it is precisely this simple decision that organizes the entire experience of the project: living close to the earth, yet suspended above it.

item.title: São João Pharmacy / Tsou Arquitectos
item.dc:creator: Pilar Caballero
item.description:
Form
The building takes on a clear, contained volume, distinguished by the curvilinear form of its façade — a gesture that follows the profile of the street and marks the building's presence on the corner it occupies. This curvature is not merely a plastic device: it is the element that functionally sets the volume apart from the surrounding residential fabric, giving it its own identity without breaking with the scale of the context. The composition is organised over two floors above ground level, complemented by a technical basement, resulting in a compact mass that reads clearly from the street.

item.title: Breeze House / Ábaton
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: Breeze House is a new construction project in Madrid that includes the most fundamental aspects of the ABATON philosophy. A modern house framed in nature and light that takes advantage of the characteristics of a plot with great potential to create a house that blends with its exterior.

item.title: What is Blue Infrastructure? Rethinking Water's Role in City Design
item.dc:creator: Olivia Poston
item.description: Nature-based solutions are a primary strategy for contemporary climate adaptation and urban ecological resilience, embraced by cities regardless of their geography or climate zone. Green roofs, urban forests, bioswales, expanding tree canopy, protected wetlands, and permeable landscapes are featured prominently in municipal adaptation plans. These interventions are deployed across neighborhoods, distributed through street networks, and measured by hectares restored, trees planted, stormwater retained, or temperatures reduced. This shift expands the role of ecology within cities, establishing environmental elements as infrastructure systems and providing planners with a grounded framework for integrating natural systems into urban development.

item.title: Antiquity exhibition at Wawel castle / NArchitekTURA
item.dc:creator: Nina Vuga
item.description: The design of the exhibition 'Masterpieces from the Lanckoroński Collection: A Story of Antiquity' is an attempt to introduce unconventional, modern display methods into the historic architecture of Wawel. The concept is based on a stylistically cohesive arrangement of all the rooms, consistent in form but varied in the selection of colours and materials. This, in turn, creates an element of surprise and a gradual progression of impressions.

item.title: Shanghai Guohua Heyuejia International Senior Living Centre, Continuing Care Retirement Community / GN Architects
item.dc:creator: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang
item.description: Guohua Heyuejia International Senior Living Centre is located in Taopu Smart City, Putuo District, Shanghai. The project responds to a long-standing pattern in China's senior living sector, where large, low-density communities have often been developed in suburban locations. Although these projects may offer access to nature, they can also separate older residents from family visits, public services and familiar social networks. Guohua Heyuejia therefore begins with a different proposition: senior living should return to the city and remain connected to everyday urban life.

item.title: Yaku – Sustainable Urban Runoff Management Module / El Sindicato Arquitectura
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: Isla Tortuga Park, located in northern Quito, Ecuador, was selected for the implementation of the Yaku (meaning "water" in Kichwa) prototype. This modular urban furniture project blends public space with sustainable rainwater and biodiversity management. Designed to be installed on any surface, its objective is to capture rainwater, store it, and promote its infiltration into the ground, emulating the natural water cycle. Yaku invites people to gather in public spaces while raising awareness about the vital relationship between water and the city.

item.title: MFA House / Simone Jazbik Arquitetura
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: Located in Búzios, Rio de Janeiro, on a 943 m² plot within a gated community, this 348 m² beach house was designed from scratch by @SimoneJazbik.Arq. Designed for a couple in their late 50s—both lawyers—and their two daughters, this is the fourth residence the firm has designed for the family, who are long-time clients. Initially intended for weekends and seasonal rentals, the house has since become central to the owners' routine, as they now split their time between Búzios and Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Casa Pura Vida / Zozaya Arquitectos
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: Pura Vida was born from the clients' desire to create a unique residence in Troncones: a contemporary home that leverages Mexico's construction qualities, from the richness of its materials to the precision of its artisanal craftsmanship.

item.title: Epitácio 3714 Building / Cité Arquitetura
item.dc:creator: Susanna Moreira
item.description: Situated on one of the most singular plots of land in Rio de Janeiro's South Zone, the Epitácio building overlooks the Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon, making the surrounding environment the protagonist of the design. Developed by Cité Arquitetura, the residential building translates a contemplative and fluid atmosphere into architecture, inspired by the passage of time and a sensitive relationship with the natural landscape.

item.title: HUT-SPOT Pavilion / m²ft architects
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: HUT-SPOT stands on the edge of the forest, where the vegetation of the Romagna hills in Italy is gradually reclaiming an asphalt clearing, a former tennis court abandoned for decades. It is a threshold between two worlds with different logics. Here, at this point of transition between the artificial and nature reclaiming its space, the pavilion finds its meaning, gathering pruning waste and dry branches from the forest into a modular structure that forms a zigurat within a parallelepiped grid: a layering of waste that is both primitive and contemporary.

item.title: Construction of a Media Library and Redesign of a Music School in Sarlat-la-Canéda / Dominique Coulon & associés
item.dc:creator: Valeria Silva
item.description: The media library and music school are built against an ochre cliff, which gives them unique character. The aim here was to place a modern construction in one of Europe's most beautiful medieval towns, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and characterized by the golden hue of its maze of quaint alleyways with old townhouses.

item.title: 12 Colombian Houses Featuring Exposed Brick
item.dc:creator: Santiago Baraya
item.description: Brick is one of Colombia's most widely used materials, helping its local architecture stand out globally. This is due to the excellent quality of the clay found in several regions of the country. In addition to cladding most of the buildings that define Bogota's urban landscape, the material is used in all its forms, from adobe to floor tiles in rural homes.

item.title: Ocean Stories Museum / Transborder Studio
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: Transborder designs Arctic Ocean museum in wood, aluminum, and local stone.

item.title: “Art Is Not Fiction, but a Surplus Reality:” Pedro Reyes on Sculpture as Social Practice in Louisiana Channel Interview
item.dc:creator: Reyyan Dogan
item.description: Mexican sculptor Pedro Reyes has developed a multidisciplinary practice that spans sculpture, architecture, social engagement, and activism. Trained as an architect, Reyes approaches sculpture as both a material and a collective process, combining traditional stone carving with participatory projects that address contemporary social issues. His work frequently explores transformation, whether through physical materials or community action, positioning sculpture as a tool for reimagining social realities. In a 2025 interview with Louisiana Channel, Reyes discusses the influence of architecture on his artistic practice, the concept of "social sculpture," and the importance of preserving craft traditions in an increasingly automated world.
